opening_message:
Ticket 1: Matthew Mejia (employee ID E034) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E034.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Matthew Mejia (E034) is a full-time Analyst. Requested write access to Payroll. As full-time employee, max is write (admin requires owning role; Analyst does not own Payroll). Requested level equals maximum, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E034 (Matthew Mejia) is a contractor with basic security training (prior note claiming full-time conflicts). Contractors max is read; write requires advanced training. Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read for Payroll.
reason: Employment type is an HR fact: HR's database lookup shows Matthew Mejia (E034) is a full-time employee. As a full-time employee, the maximum access to Payroll is write (admin requires the role to own the system, and Analyst does not own Payroll). The requested level is write, which equals the maximum, so write is granted. (Note: the Security note claims contractor status, but HR is the authoritative source for employment type; even so, granting write does not exceed the full-time maximum and does not exceed the requested level.)
